sections.leaf: Alternate, simple, ovate to obovate, 2 to 5 inches long, with 3 to 7 bristle tipped irregular lobes, base broadly wedge-shaped; dark green and shiny above, paler below with tufts of pubescence in the vein axils; turning red in the fall.
sections.flower: Species is monoecious; male flowers borne on 2 to 4 inch long pale reddish green catkins; reddish females borne on very short axillary spikes, appears with the leaves in mid-spring.
sections.fruit: Dark brown striated acorn, 1/3 to 1/2 inch long; saucer-shaped cap covers 1/3 of the nut, cap scales are tightly appressed, matures in the fall after two growing seasons.
sections.twig: Red-brown, glabrous; buds red-brown, ovoid, generally glabrous but may have some pubescence on the tips of the bud scales, with multiple end buds.
sections.bark: Gray-brown, initially smooth, becoming ridged and furrowed.
sections.form: A large shrub or a small tree to 50 feet, but more commonly less than 30 feet.

sections.terminal_buds: red-brown, ovoid to subconic, 2.5-5 mm, glabrous or scales somewhat ciliate.
sections.leaves: petiole 6-23 mm, glabrous or with a few persistent hairs.
sections.leaf_blade: broadly ovate to elliptic or obovate, 40-130 × 20-90 mm, base cuneate to obtuse, margins with 3-5(-7) oblong lobes and up to 10 awns, apex acute; surfaces abaxially glabrous except for conspicuous axillary tufts of tomentum, veins raised, adaxially planar, glabrous.
sections.acorns: biennial; cup thin, saucer-shaped, 4-6 mm high × 9-14 mm wide, covering 1/3 nut, outer surface puberulent, inner surface glabrous or with a few hairs around scar, scale tips appressed, acute; nut globose or ovoid, 9-14 × 9-14 mm, glabrous, scar diam. 4-7.5 mm.

sources.text: Trees , deciduous, to 15 m. Bark gray to light brown, scaly. Twigs deep red, 1-2 mm diam., glabrous. sources.distribution: Flowering spring. Granitic outcrops and dry slopes and knolls; 50-500 m; Ala., Ga., S.C.
